group: bouncer with a counter in a fixed wall
title: What is known about 1RB---_1LC0RF_1LD0LC_0RE0LF_0RD1LA_1RB0LE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB---_1LC0RF_1LD0LC_0RE0LF_0RD1LA_1RB0LE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The head bounces between a block that grows at the left end and a wall of exactly 1,573 cells at the right end. The wall is a counter, now decoded: 46 digits of 25 cells, 15 trips of the head per sweep and a carry table of 73 entries, which reproduces every sweep to 2·1010 steps. The carries reach the end of the wall only near 1038 steps; what happens then is the question.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (A1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 34,610 cells have been visited and 20,724 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.494). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).

claims.title: A wall of fixed length that counts
claims.text: After 2·107 steps the tape at each sweep is C>0 (01101)^n W with W exactly 1,573 cells and n growing by one per four sweeps. Consecutive walls differ from cell 44 on; the deepest change reaches cells 252, 294, 319, 344, 369 at sweeps 274, 406, 2,296, 7,335, 20,772 (by 1010 steps).

claims.title: A wall of fixed length that counts
claims.text: After 2·107 steps the tape at each sweep is C>0 (01101)^n W with W exactly 1,573 cells and n growing by about one per sweep. Consecutive walls differ from cell 44 on; the deepest change reaches cells 252, 294, 319, 344, 369 at sweeps 274, 406, 2,296, 7,335, 20,772 (by 1010 steps).

claims.title: Size of the tape description (family screen)
claims.text: At the 4 records between 2.6·10<sup>8</sup> and 1.6·10<sup>10</sup> steps (first new leftmost or rightmost cell after each threshold 10<sup>6</sup>·4^k) the tape has 17,886 to 137,401 visited cells and compresses to 146 to 176 level-2 tokens (repeats of a word of at most 40 cells, then repeats of groups of such tokens).

claims.title: Proposed family: F06, block-list counters
claims.text: During the present epoch the description of the tape does not grow: 146 to 176 level-2 tokens at the four left-end records from 2.6·108 to 1.6·1010 steps, and in the macro simulator (blocks of 5 cells) exactly 314 runs at each of 80 sampled left-end records from 3·107 to 1016 steps. Only the block (11010)^n grows. The wall is a counter with digits of 25 cells. After its first 44 cells, each of the first 40 digits has the form x110 x110 x011 0011 0x11 0x11 0 at every one of 2,819 sweeps (steps 2·107 to 3·108): five free cells per digit. The first digit returns to the same contents every 8 sweeps, the first two digits together every 64 sweeps and the first three every 512 sweeps, taking 8, 64 and 512 different values (py/digits.py). The deepest digit changed by a sweep is digit 2 on 1,336 sweeps, digit 3 on 782, digit 4 on 326, digit 5 on 124, and so on down to digit 11 once. The counter has overflowed before. At the left-end record at step 1,428,412 the tape was (11010)^244 followed by about 240 cells that end in 16 eight-cell words. No new cell was added at the left end for the next three million steps, and at the next left-end record (step 4,487,735) the block was gone, a 25-cell word 0101100110111001100110111 stood 45 times in a row (new digits, all equal) and the tape ended in 30 eight-cell words. So the machine is a counter that is rebuilt longer when it overflows, with the block as its clock, and the next overflow is far beyond simulation. That is the shape of the counter families (F06), not of a bounded engine (F01): the wall is bounded only within an epoch.

claims.title: One halting question for two machines (the shifted runs)
claims.text: 1RB0RA_0LC0RF_0LB1RD_1LE---_1RA0LF_1LE0RC is the table of 1RB---_1LC0RF_1LD0LC_0RE0LF_0RD1LA_1RB0LE mirrored, with the states renamed, started in state C. After 2 and 49 steps the two runs are at the same configuration, except that the second has the word 10001101 once more at the right end. Two tapes that differ only by k such words just right of a cell q, with blank tape beyond q in the first, make the same moves until the head moves right from q. In state B on a 1 the head crosses the k words and comes back with the same cells, for every k (far_B); q then moves two cells to the right. With the renaming and the mirror proved as well: if in the run of 1RB---_1LC0RF_1LD0LC_0RE0LF_0RD1LA_1RB0LE the head moves right from the rightmost cell visited so far only in state B on a 1 (from step 2 on), then it halts from blank tape if and only if 1RB0RA_0LC0RF_0LB1RD_1LE---_1RA0LF_1LE0RC does (two_machines). The condition is proved (next claim).

claims.title: The condition is proved: the right end grows only through far_B
claims.text: Good30773 is a fact about the last four cells of the tape, q−3 to q, and not about the rebuilds of the counter. Keep only those four cells and the state, and forget everything left of them: with the head inside the window, the state, the cells left of the head in the window and the cells from the head to q; with the head further left, the four cells only, and let the head come back in any state that a move right can produce (B, D, E or F). Starting from step 2 this over-approximation has exactly 32 abstract configurations (30 with the head in the window, 2 outside it; whenever the head is left of the window the last three cells read 101). None of them moves right from q except in state B on a 1, and the set is closed under a step (closed, by decide). So the condition holds for every number of steps (good30773), and 1RB---_1LC0RF_1LD0LC_0RE0LF_0RD1LA_1RB0LE halts from blank tape if and only if 1RB0RA_0LC0RF_0LB1RD_1LE---_1RA0LF_1LE0RC does (two_machines'), with no condition.

claims.title: One halting question for two machines: a second proof, in Coq (busycoq)
claims.text: The same equivalence, proved independently on top of busycoq's definitions: TailWord.eqv : halts tm c0 <-> halts tm' c0 with 1RB0RA_0LC0RF_0LB1RD_1LE---_1RA0LF_1LE0RC on the other side. A model configuration is read as a configuration of either machine (the second with the word 10001101 after the rightmost visited cell); its invariant is a window of the last four cells with 28 abstract configurations, closed under the abstract step (check_S0, one vm_compute). Print Assumptions TailWord.eqv: closed under the global context. Compiles in about 2.4 s with Coq 8.20.1 (busycoq's version) and with 8.18.0; changing the extra word, one transition, or one entry of the invariant makes it fail.

claims.title: The condition holds in the first 10<sup>11</sup> steps (now proved for all steps)
claims.text: In the first 1011 steps of the run of 1RB---_1LC0RF_1LD0LC_0RE0LF_0RD1LA_1RB0LE the head moves right from the rightmost visited cell 100 times, always in state B on a 1, and all before step 4.5·106, while the counter in the wall was rebuilt after its first overflows; afterwards the right end of the tape does not move. At 270,284 visits of the head to the left end in state C, the tape of the run from C is the tape of the run from A followed by 10001101. Proving the condition needs the theory of the counter's rebuild.

claims.title: The digit carry rule
claims.text: The wall is a head part of 44 cells, 46 digits a110 b110 c011 0011 0d11 0e11 0 and an end part of 139 cells. Each sweep is 15 trips from the head part into the digits; trips 1, 6, 11 feed carry Y, the others carry X, and a table of 73 entries (carries X, Y, P, Q, R) gives what a carry does to a digit. The table reproduces all 4,500 trips of the first 300 sweeps (machine simulated step by step) and all 29,299 sweeps from 2·107 to 2·1010 steps.

claims.title: The carry table never gets stuck (a theorem about the model)
claims.text: On digit strings whose neighbours are among 240 allowed pairs, each trip of the table lands on such a string again and never meets a pair (carry, digit) outside the 73 entries, for strings of every length; from the 46 digits of the wall at step 20,018,306 the table never gets stuck, at any number of trips, until a carry runs off the last digit. About the table only: its link to the machine is the simulation above.

claims.title: When the carries reach the end of the wall
claims.text: In 10<sup>6</sup> sweeps of the table, a quarter of the trips pass digit 0 and from digit 4 on each digit is reached by 3/8 of the trips that reach the one before. At that rate the carries pass digit 45 about once in 6·10<sup>19</sup> trips, near 10<sup>38</sup> steps. Forced carries on made-up walls show the end part counting in a fresh form and, after 56 carries, rewritten with the far end one word longer; no halt in 400.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The decider pipeline of bbchallenge left it open; no proof either way is recorded here yet.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0RA_0LC0RF_0LB1RD_1LE---_1RA0LF_1LE0RC up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The head bounces between a block that grows at the left end and a wall of exactly 1,573 cells at the right end. The wall is a counter, now decoded: 46 digits of 25 cells, 15 trips of the head per sweep and a carry table of 73 entries, which reproduces every sweep to 2·1010 steps. The carries reach the end of the wall only near 1038 steps; what happens then is the question. It is proved to share that question with 1RB0RA_0LC0RF_0LB1RD_1LE---_1RA0LF_1LE0RC: one halts exactly when the other does.

facts.text: It halts from blank tape if and only if 1RB0RA_0LC0RF_0LB1RD_1LE---_1RA0LF_1LE0RC does: proved in Lean and in Coq (below).
the carry table of the counter, checked on every sweep to 2·1010 steps (below).
No halt in the C simulator; 34,610 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.

sections.heading: A counter inside a fixed wall
html: The left part of the tape is the word 01101 repeated, about one more copy per sweep. The right part is a wall that has had exactly 1,573 cells since 2·107 steps: the right end of the tape never moves.

The wall is different after every sweep, but not at random. Comparing one wall with the next, the changes always start at the same cell, 44, and usually stay within a hundred cells; only now and then do they reach further, and each new depth (25 cells further each time) is reached about three times later than the previous one. That is how the carries of a counter behave: digits about 25 cells wide, in a base near 3.
About 46 such digits are in the wall. The next section decodes them: the exact carry rule, which you can run.

sections.heading: The digit carry rule
sections.html:
The wall is now decoded. Write it as H D0 D1 … D45 E (10001101)30: a head part H of 44 cells that is the same at every sweep, 46 digits of 25 cells, an end part E of 139 cells, and the words at the far end. Every digit has the form a110 b110 c011 0011 0d11 0e11 0, so it is five free cells a b c d e; below, each digit is a column of five squares, a at the top.

Between two visits to the left end the head does not make one pass over the counter but 15 trips: from H into the digits and back. H is a fixed sequencer: trip 1, 6 and 11 of every sweep feed the carry Y into digit 0, the other twelve feed X. A carry that reaches a digit rewrites it and either stops or passes a carry on to the next digit, and five carries occur: X, Y, P, Q, R. That is the whole rule: one table of 73 entries. X is binary counting in a b c (a lowest); when all three are 1 the digit overflows, and d e records how often it has (11 → 01 → 10), which decides the carry passed on.

The table

d>d': the carry turns digit d into d' and stops; d>d':c: … and passes c on (blue). The entries of the last trip are outlined.

How deep the carries go

The digits start as they were at step 20,018,306. Step through a few trips, then run 10,000 sweeps and look at the counts: a quarter of all trips go past digit 0, and from digit 4 on each digit is reached by 3/8 of the trips that reach the one before (the ratio column settles at 2.667). The button Run the next sweep on the machine runs the Turing machine itself on the same wall, 5,000 to 15,000 steps, and compares the wall it leaves with the table's.

What is established, and how. The table reproduces every one of the 4,500 trips of the first 300 sweeps and every one of the 29,299 sweeps from step 2·107 to 2·1010, simulated in C and Python (py/carry.py): computed, not proved. Lean proves, kernel only, that the table never needs an entry it does not have: on the strings of digits whose neighbours are among 240 allowed pairs (and whose digit 0 is one of 8 values for each trip), every trip lands on such a string again, for strings of any length, and the 46 digits of step 20,018,306 are such a string (lean/Carry.lean, trip_good, wall0_never_stuck). That is a theorem about the table, not yet about the machine.

At 3/8 per digit the carries pass digit 45 about once in 6·1019 trips, near 1038 steps. Forcing carries into E on made-up walls (py/endregion.py) shows that E is more counter in a fresh form (its cells 0, 4, 8 count in binary), and that after 56 such carries it is rewritten and the far end grows by one word: no halt in 400 of them. What the run does when its own carries get there is the open question.

sections.heading: Two tables that are one machine
sections.html:
Two of the 608 holdouts are one halting question. Call 1RB---_1LC0RF_1LD0LC_0RE0LF_0RD1LA_1RB0LE (this page) the first machine and 1RB0RA_0LC0RF_0LB1RD_1LE---_1RA0LF_1LE0RC (its page) the second machine. It is proved, in Lean and again in Coq, that the first halts from blank tape if and only if the second does. That does not say whether either one halts: it says that the list of open machines is one shorter than it looks. The next five sections show why, and let you check each piece in the browser.

It starts with the tables. Point at (or tap) any cell of one table and the matching cell of the other lights up: the same symbol is written, the direction is reversed, and the states are renamed A→D, B→E, C→A, D→B, E→C, F→F. So the second machine is the first one watched in a mirror, with different names on the states. The one real difference is where it starts: the second machine's A is the first machine's C.

Renaming the second table's states back and exchanging left and right gives the first table exactly, the halting cell included (the green table). The machines differ only in the state they start in: C instead of A.

A different start state usually means a different run, and the related-machines screen found no common configuration in the first 107 steps. But it compared the runs step for step. The next section compares them event for event.

sections.heading: One run, watched in a mirror
sections.html:
Run both machines from blank tape. After 2 steps of the first and 49 of the second, the two tapes are the same when the second is read in a mirror, except that the second has one more word, 10001101, at the far right end. From then on each step of one is a step of the other, with one exception. When the head moves right from q, the rightmost cell visited so far, it crosses the end of the tape. The first machine does that in 5 steps; the second has to cross the extra word too and takes 49. Call one step of both, or one crossing, a model step. Below, the two runs are drawn on the model-step clock, the second one mirrored. The pictures are the same except for the extra word on the right (blue band), and the head (orange) is always in the same place.

first machine, 1RB---_1LC0RF_1LD0LC_0RE0LF_0RD1LA_1RB0LE
second machine in a mirror, 1RB0RA_0LC0RF_0LB1RD_1LE---_1RA0LF_1LE0RC
1headthe extra word 10001101time runs down; one row per model step (sampled)

Runs both machines in your browser and compares the whole tapes at every crossing.

This is Computed evidence for a few million steps; the C program c/lockstep.c checked 1011 steps (270,284 visits to the left end). The proof that it lasts for ever has two parts: the crossing itself (next section) and the fact that the head never leaves q in any other way (the section after).

sections.heading: Crossing the far end: 5 steps against 49
sections.html:
Here is the one place where the two runs come apart for a moment, drawn in the first machine's frame (the second machine's run is this, mirrored). Both lanes start from the same configuration of the real run, just before its third crossing: state B on the 1 at q (green outline). The lower lane has k extra words after q (blue). The slider moves both lanes together; the upper one takes 5 steps, the lower one 44k + 5.

Whatever k is, the head walks right through the words, turns at the blank end and walks back, and both lanes end in state D one cell left of q with 1 0 1 written from q on: q has moved two cells right and the extra words moved with it. Lean proves this for every k (far_B, 44k + 5 steps, in lean/FarEnd.lean); Coq needs only k = 0 and k = 1 (far0, far1, each checked by running the machine).

sections.heading: Four cells that settle it
sections.html:
Could the head ever leave q in some other state, or on a 0? Then the first machine would step onto a blank cell while the second steps onto the extra word, and the runs would part. The proof rules this out by looking only at the last four cells of the tape, q−3 to q, the window, and forgetting everything to their left. A card below is one abstract configuration: the four cells, and the state and head position when the head is in the window. When the head is further left (card out) even the state is forgotten, and the head may come back in any state that a move to the right can produce: B, D, E or F.

From the start there are exactly 28 of them, and none moves right from q except in state B on a 1 (green cards: the crossing). Click a card to see where one step can lead (blue): always to another card. That closure is the whole invariant; Coq checks it with one vm_compute (check_S0).

The window works because the left end of the tape cannot reach it unseen. When the head leaves the window to the left, the window's last three cells always read 1 0 1 (the two out cards), and whatever the counter does far to the left, the head can only come back through the window's first cell. The window is a deliberately coarse picture, an over-approximation: it allows more than the machine does, so if even the coarse picture never leaves q the wrong way, the real run cannot. The Lean proof uses a slightly finer window with 32 configurations (lean/RightEnd.lean, closed by decide); the Coq proof was written on its own and lands on 28.

sections.heading: Checked in Coq, step by step
sections.html:
The Coq proof is one file of 371 lines, coq/Eqv_TailWord.v, built on the definitions of busycoq, the Coq library in which the bbchallenge results are checked. It is meant for busycoq itself, in the style of its Eqv_WordPairs.v. Its steps, from the machines to the theorem:

  1. The mirrorEvery transition of the second table is the first's with the direction reversed and the states renamed by g. tm'_some, tm'_none; 12 cases.
  2. One model for both runsA configuration Cfg keeps the window apart from the rest of the tape. to_config false reads it as a configuration of the first machine; to_config true as the mirrored configuration of the second, with W8 = 10001101 after q.
  3. The model stepf is one step of both machines, or the crossing at the far end. far0 (5 steps) and far1 (49 steps) are run by busycoq's execute. f_spec: each model step is at least one step of whichever machine you read it as, and a model halt is a halt of both.
  4. The invariantP c: the window of c is one of the 28 cards of S0. check_S0 (one vm_compute) shows the list is closed under the abstract step and that no card leaves q except B on a 1; anext_spec shows the abstract step covers the real one.
  5. The startinit0, init1: from blank tape the first machine reaches the model's start in 2 steps, the second in 49.
  6. The theorembusycoq's halts_iff turns the model into halts (machine b) c0 <-> iter_halts f cfg0 for both b, so TailWord.eqv : halts tm c0 <-> halts tm' c0.
Coq 8.20.1busycoq's own version. The core up to Individual62.v, then the file: 2.4 s, no warnings of its own. Also checked on Coq 8.18.0.
No axiomsPrint Assumptions TailWord.eqv: Closed under the global context.
It can failChanging the word W8, one transition of the second machine, or removing one card from S0 each makes the file fail to compile.
Two proofsThe Lean proof (two_machines' in lean/Lockstep.lean with good30773 in lean/RightEnd.lean) came first; the Coq file is an independent second proof, with its own invariant.

Kernel The two machines halt together. Open Whether they halt. The Coq file is on a branch of a fork of busycoq (Eqv_TailWord.v), ready to be proposed upstream; it has not been submitted or reviewed there yet. If it is merged, bbchallenge can count these two holdouts as one.

Build it yourself: sh holdouts/1RB---_1LC0RF_1LD0LC_0RE0LF_0RD1LA_1RB0LE/coq/build.sh /path/to/busycoq with a checkout of busycoq's BB6 branch and Coq 8.20.1 (or 8.18).

sections.heading: Which family it belongs to
html: The 22 machines of family F09 (“bouncers over lists of counters, not yet classified”) were screened in one way. The machine runs from blank tape for 2·1010 steps; each time the tape reaches a new cell after a threshold, the tape is compressed twice: first repeats of one word, then repeats of groups of words. If the tape is a few growing blocks and a bounded rest, the number of level-2 tokens stays bounded while the tape grows. Everything in this section is observed in one run. None of it is proved.
Proposed family: F06, block-list counters (a counter in a wall that is rebuilt longer at each overflow, with a growing block as its clock).

During the present epoch the description of the tape does not grow: 146 to 176 level-2 tokens at the four left-end records from 2.6·108 to 1.6·1010 steps, and in the macro simulator (blocks of 5 cells) exactly 314 runs at each of 80 sampled left-end records from 3·107 to 1016 steps. Only the block (11010)^n grows.

The wall is a counter with digits of 25 cells. After its first 44 cells, each of the first 40 digits has the form x110 x110 x011 0011 0x11 0x11 0 at every one of 2,819 sweeps (steps 2·107 to 3·108): five free cells per digit. The first digit returns to the same contents every 8 sweeps, the first two digits together every 64 sweeps and the first three every 512 sweeps, taking 8, 64 and 512 different values (py/digits.py). The deepest digit changed by a sweep is digit 2 on 1,336 sweeps, digit 3 on 782, digit 4 on 326, digit 5 on 124, and so on down to digit 11 once.

The counter has overflowed before. At the left-end record at step 1,428,412 the tape was (11010)^244 followed by about 240 cells that end in 16 eight-cell words. No new cell was added at the left end for the next three million steps, and at the next left-end record (step 4,487,735) the block was gone, a 25-cell word 0101100110111001100110111 stood 45 times in a row (new digits, all equal) and the tape ended in 30 eight-cell words. So the machine is a counter that is rebuilt longer when it overflows, with the block as its clock, and the next overflow is far beyond simulation. That is the shape of the counter families (F06), not of a bounded engine (F01): the wall is bounded only within an epoch.

Next step. Decode the five cells of a digit into a carry rule (a transducer on digits), prove it with symtm, and work out the rebuild; then the question is whether the rebuild can go wrong for some length of the block.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.494). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 34,610 cells (25,368 left of the start, 201 right), with a density of 1s of 0.599.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. In the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other's at the same step, even up to a shift of the tape. Compared at matching visits instead, they are one run seen in a mirror, the second with one more word at the far end, and it is proved that the two halt together or not at all (Lean: two_machines', Coq: TailWord.eqv; see the section "One halting question for two machines").
